A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, equations, and complete Appendices A and B. Retained material can be matched despite figure renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original curvature-bias measurements, conjugate-gradient experiments, and Laplace-approximation evaluations, including additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CG batch-size results, ViT Little evaluations, and measured Laplace-approximation runtimes.

M1.justification: The two-batch CG and K-FAC Laplace debiasing algorithms remain unchanged in Section 4.2 and Appendix A. New implementation and memory discussions do not establish a change to the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: The CIFAR, corrupted-CIFAR, and ImageNet task coverage is retained. ImageNet was already evaluated with ResNet-50 in v1 Figure 15; adding ViT Little changes the model configuration, not the dataset or task requirements.

E2.justification: CG retains its standard single-batch and full-batch comparisons. Laplace evaluations retain the vanilla model, single-batch K-FAC LA, and full-batch LA. The added experiments introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix B.5 adds CG batch sizes 512 and 2048, with debiased batches of 256 and 1024, alongside the existing 1024-versus-two-512 setting. B.6 adds a ViT Little configuration and a timing protocol covering K-FAC construction, debiasing, and sampling 40 weights, excluding predictive evaluation.

E4.justification: New Figure 13 tests whether CG stability persists across batch sizes. Appendices B.5–B.6 also add targeted runtime and memory analyses, including the runtime breakdown in Figure 18. Existing corruption, curvature-proxy, training-stage, and model-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Figure 18 reports runtime means over five runs with error bars covering one standard deviation. Existing five-mini-batch experiments and LA mean/minimum/maximum reporting remain unchanged; no increase in their run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 5 replaces the plotted CG trajectories under the same stated settings, retaining the stability conclusion. New Figures 13, 17, and 18 add CG batch-size outcomes, ViT Little accuracy/NLL/ECE results, and LA timings. Other matched result plots are retained, including the existing ResNet-50 evaluation.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, CG algorithm, and bias proofs remain unchanged. Appendix A, including the efficient CG recurrence and blockwise K-FAC derivations, is identical apart from headers.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying mini-batch geometric bias, explaining it theoretically, demonstrating its consequences, and proposing two-batch corrections. The added experimental evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly discloses that the current CG implementation uses two GGN-vector products per debiased magnitude and therefore provides no measured runtime comparison. B.6 qualifies resource claims through blockwise memory accounting and explicitly excludes the shared, expensive predictive-evaluation stage from timings.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the ViT Little checkpoint, NAdamW pretraining, and configuration links. It also discloses the naive CG implementation and quantifies memory requirements: approximately 11.1 MB extra for efficient CG, and K-FAC debiasing overhead of 91.87 MB naively versus 24.18 MB with blockwise processing.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Dosovitskiy et al. Vision Transformer reference for the new model evaluation. Section 5 and the positioning relative to alternative two-batch approaches, EKFAC, and moving averages remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are preserved. v2 adds acknowledgments, an ImageNet-results signpost in Section 6.2, and localized appendix explanations, while updating the conference header and supplementary-material terminology.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multi-batch-size CG display, ViT performance plots, and stacked runtime chart in Figures 13, 17, and 18. Retained appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, while the overall visual format remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The added batch-size tests and ViT results strengthen empirical support, while LA timings and implementation disclosures make computational claims easier to assess. These are useful, targeted gains. Runtime validation remains incomplete: CG parity is not measured, and LA timings exclude predictive evaluation.
